did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ecclesiastes opens the chapter by stating that there is a time for everything and a season for every activity under heaven.
Did you know? The first eight verses present a series of contrasts in human life, including birth and death, planting and uprooting, weeping and laughter, and love and hate.
Did you know? After listing the various seasons, Ecclesiastes asks what gain people have from their work, shifting from a description of the order of time to the question of the meaning of labor.
Did you know? According to Ecclesiastes, God has made everything beautiful in its time, but people cannot fully understand what God has done from beginning to end.
Did you know? Ecclesiastes presents joy and doing good throughout life as a practical conclusion.
Did you know? Ecclesiastes emphasizes that God’s work endures forever, and nothing can be added to it or taken away from it; this is so that people will fear God.
Did you know? Ecclesiastes describes a situation in which wickedness is found precisely where justice and righteousness should be, pointing to the gap between a place’s purpose and the reality there.

Did you know? Although wickedness is found in the place of judgment, Ecclesiastes declares that God will judge both the righteous and the wicked, and that there is a time for every matter and every deed.
Did you know? Ecclesiastes compares the fate of humans with that of animals in regard to death: both die, and both have the same breath, according to the chapter’s description.
Did you know? The chapter emphasizes the common material origin of humans and animals: everything comes from dust, and everything returns to dust.
